chunks: And what is wrong with me that I should not worship He who created me, and to whom you will be returned?
ai.seo_question: Why should one worship Allah according to Surah Yaseen?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as the voice of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) or a paradigmatic believer demonstrating *tawhid* through logical deduction (*aql*) rather than mere imitation. It underscores the dual aspects of divine sovereignty: creation (*fatarani*) and resurrection (*turja'un*), establishing the inevitability of accountability. This rhetorical structure serves as a foundational argument for monotheism, linking the origin of existence directly to its ultimate return.
